verdicts.summary: Lean has a weaker form of it. The Lean proves the display only for fields of the separated form F_γ(x,Y) = physicalMask D L q x · covered (nativeIndex h L.1) f Y, i.e. a slow mask supported in K_γ times a periodized fast field with support f ⊆ R⁺_γ; the paper assumes only the joint condition supp F_γ ⊂ K_γ × 𝓡^{abs,+}_γ on an otherwise arbitrary family, which is strictly more general (an arbitrary function supported in a product set need not factor). The Lean also carries hypotheses the display does not print: 1 ≤ L.1, 1 ≤ M.1 (band index at least one, the paper's ℓ ≥ ℓ₀) and 0 < q, and it works on (q, x, Y) with no θ variable, so the paper's qualifier 'supports taken in (r,z,t,Y) uniformly in θ' has no counterpart in this statement. The general implication is nevertheless three lines from the same stated ingredients: at a point where both factors are nonzero, masks_force_adjacency gives SlotColoring.Adj D L M from the two slow supports meeting, SlotSystem.disjoint then makes the two lifted slots disjoint, and covered_support places the fast factors in them — so the mathematics of the display is present and only the generality of the quantifier over F_γ is narrowed. I searched for a declaration stating the implication for an arbitrary family (grep of decls.jsonl for cross_product/cross_term/mul_eq_zero and for *_disjoint in the NavierStokes namespace, and the Lemma 6.1 candidate list) and found none.
